title: 第一卷 南域篇 第19章 佛道孰为顶第一卷 南域篇 第20章 玄玉一掌摧金铁
slug: 剑问九州第1286章星域虫潮
content_zh:
“无量一剑！”老道气运藏锋，锵然一剑飞出，势如飞虹，直取那僧人头颅。
饶是过去百年的残影，可惊人气势，仍让白泽感到毕露杀机！
“大慈悲掌。”老僧一掌拍出，手掌金光灿灿，宛如金铸，弥漫浩荡佛气！
隐约之间，白泽竟听到天外佛号。
那一掌，洗尽铅华。那一剑，浑然天成。
“轰！！——”
高手过招，只在刹那。
两人初一交手，僧人倒退三步，藏锋剑飞射出去，锵然钉入石壁。
碎石飞溅，山洞摇摇欲坠。若非早知这是残影，此刻白泽二人早已吓得抱头鼠窜。
“剑九，沧海一笑！”老道佩剑被震飞，并不后退，反而上前一步，衣袖一摆，纵横剑气如海浪狂卷，呼拥而出！
“沧海一笑？！”欧阳木忽然大叫一声，像是想起什么江湖隐秘。
白泽只觉得窒息。
那一袖的剑气，一眼看来，竟然比谢玄当日的拂柳一剑更为可怕！若同是松岗，恐怕这老道一袖，那山岗夷为平地不说，还要在地上留下一个百丈大坑！
“阿弥陀佛！”老僧气定神闲，双手合十，体运浩荡佛气，一口浑厚金钟顿时出现在洞窟之中，将他团团包裹。
“佛门秘技，金钟罩！”白泽双眼放光。
“铛！！——”
强横无匹的钟声，在如海剑气撞上金钟的刹那响起，声势远盛牛鬼一吼，直如炸雷在耳边轰鸣！
“噗！”白泽一口血喷了出来，灵魂都在颤抖，当场倒了下去，只觉得好像有一个巨大的石碾在碾压他的精神。
欧阳木更干脆，两眼一闭，面如金纸，直接昏死过去。
山窟震荡，地动山摇！

“玄玉掌！”老道变招，右手漆黑如墨，凌空一掌拍了过去，直接将老僧金钟拍得四分五裂。
“金刚菩提！”老僧一声大喝，周身金光四溢，一串佛珠在掌中，捏佛门狮子印，迎面对了上去。
“轰！！——”
白泽再也撑不住，一口血又喷出来，直接昏死过去。
只是残影，残招影现，尚且如此，如果真的观战，岂非即刻粉身碎骨？
灵魂沉寂的时间，白泽恍惚间听到一声疲惫的叹息，仿佛穿越了悠久的时光，历尽沧桑。
“山高人为峰，”那人叹息，“佛道孰为顶？”
……
醒来的时候，白泽只觉得头疼欲裂。他爬了起来，山洞里那两人的残影已经消失不见。火把静静燃烧，这里流光溢彩，仿佛之前的事情从未发生过。
“山高人为峰，佛道孰为顶？”白泽看到百年前那老僧在石壁上留下的佛门一偈，沉默很久。
然后他默默拔出藏锋，笔走龙蛇，在坚硬如铁的石壁上，刻下他的回答。
“仙路无始亦无终，
唯有一剑问苍穹。
虎踞龙盘风如晦，
何来正统何为峰？”
修道之路，问仙是为顶。可仙路缥缈，谁又说得清从哪里开始，又从哪里终结呢？
我有的，只不过一剑而已。
若以此剑问苍穹，这风雨如晦的九州大地，究竟什么才是顶峰？是佛法？是道术？还是那策天下的儒门？
“这首诗，叫什么？”不知何时，欧阳木也醒了过来，问白泽。
“就叫《对老僧》吧。”白泽说。

“仙路无始亦无终，唯有一剑问苍穹。”欧阳木说，“你说得对，登顶之路，我们什么都没有，只有一剑。”
“这把断剑在这，想必是那老僧赢了。”白泽说，看着手里的藏锋，“可他在最后却不知佛道究竟何为顶。你说，这是他对那道人的尊重和缅怀，还是他真的不知道？”
content_en:
"Infinite Sword!" The old Taoist Qi Lun Hidden Edge flew out with a sword that was as powerful as a flying rainbow and went straight for the monk's head.
Even though it was an afterimage of the past hundred years, its astonishing momentum still made Bai Ze feel like he was revealing his murderous intent!
"The Palm of Great Compassion." The old monk slapped it with one palm. The palm was golden, like gold cast, filled with the mighty Buddha energy!
Vaguely, Bai Ze actually heard the name of the Buddha outside the sky.
That palm washed away the lead. That sword was completely natural.
"Boom!!——"
Masters exchange moves only in an instant.
The two exchanged blows on the first day. The monk took three steps back, and the hidden-edge sword flew out and nailed into the stone wall.
Debris flew and the cave crumbled. If they hadn't known earlier that this was an afterimage, Bai Ze and the other two would have been so frightened that they ran away with their heads in their hands.
"Jianjiu, the sea smiles!" The old Taoist sword was knocked away. Instead of retreating, he took a step forward, waved his sleeves, and the vertical and horizontal sword energy rolled out like a wild wave of waves, shouting out!
"A smile from the sea?!" Ouyang Mu suddenly shouted, as if he was remembering some secret in the world.
Bai Ze just felt suffocated.
At first glance, the sword energy in that sleeve was even more terrifying than Xie Xuan's Fu Liu Yijian back then! If they were both in the Songshan Mountains, I'm afraid that this old man would not only level the mountains to the ground, but also leave a huge hole of 100 feet in the ground!
"Amitabha!" The old monk calmed down, clasped his hands together, and channeled the mighty Buddha's energy into his body. A powerful golden bell suddenly appeared in the cave and enveloped him.
"The secret skill of Buddhism, the golden bell!" Bai Ze's eyes lit up.
"Clang!!——"
The unparalleled bell sounded at the moment when the sea of sword energy hit the golden bell. The roar of Niu Gui was so powerful that it was like thunder roaring in the ears!
"Poof!" Bai Ze spurted out a mouthful of blood, his soul was shaking, and he fell down on the spot. He felt as if a huge stone was crushing his spirit.
Ouyang Mugeng simply closed his eyes, his face was like gold paper, and he passed out.
The caves are shaking, the earth is shaking, and the mountains are shaking!
"Xuan Jade Palm!" The old Taoist changed his move, his right hand was as black as ink, and he swatted it with a palm in the air, directly smashing the old monk Jin Zhong into pieces.
"Rudraksha!" the old monk shouted, golden light overflowing from his body. He held a string of Buddhist beads in his palm, pinched the Buddha's lion seal, and faced him.
"Boom!!——"
Bai Ze couldn't hold on any longer, a mouthful of blood spurted out again, and he passed out.
It's just an afterimage, and the remaining shadow of the move is still there. If you really watch the battle, won't you be instantly shattered to pieces?
When his soul was silent, Bai Ze heard a tired sigh in a trance, as if he had traveled through a long time and experienced vicissitudes of life.
"The tallest mountain is the peak," the man sighed. "Which one, Buddha or Taoism, is the top?"
…
When he woke up, Bai Ze only felt a splitting headache. He climbed up, and the afterimages of the two people in the cave had disappeared. The torch burned quietly, and the place was filled with light, as if nothing had ever happened before.
"The highest mountain is the peak, which one is the top of Buddhism and Taoism?" Bai Ze was silent for a long time when he saw the Buddhist verse left by the old monk on the stone wall a hundred years ago.
Then he silently pulled out his Tibetan sword and carved his answer on the stone wall as hard as iron.
"The path to immortality has neither beginning nor end,
Only one sword asks the sky.
The tiger is perched and the dragon is coiled in the wind,
Where does orthodoxy come from? "
On the road of cultivating Taoism, the top step is to ask the immortals. But the path to immortality is so murky, who can tell where it begins and where it ends?
All I have is a sword.
If you ask the sky with this sword, what is the pinnacle of this windy and rainy land of Kyushu? Is it Buddhism? Is it Taoism? Or the Confucian sect who dominates the world?
"What's the name of this poem?" Ouyang Mu also woke up at some point and asked Bai Ze.
"Let's call it 'Conversation with the Old Monk'," Bai Ze said.
"The path to immortality has neither beginning nor end, only a sword reaches the sky." Ouyang Mu said, "You are right, on the way to the top, we have nothing but a sword."
"This broken sword is here. It must be the old monk who won." Bai Ze said, looking at the hidden sword in his hand, "But heIn the end, I don’t know what the Buddha’s path is. Do you think this is his respect and memory for that man, or does he really not know? "
